Below is a framework for installing monitoring cameras in shared-use spaces of an Airbnb rental.  Before you install anything, be sure to:

• Review local/state laws on video surveillance (audio recording is often more tightly regulated than video)  
• Comply with Airbnb’s policy: no hidden cameras, full disclosure of any recording devices in your listing and in-home guide  
• Never install cameras in bedrooms, bathrooms or other spaces where guests have a reasonable expectation of privacy  

1. Recommended “Discreet but Visible” Locations  
   (all in common‐area zones only)

  a. Entryway / Front Door  
     – Slimline Wi-Fi video doorbell mounted at eye level  
     – Field of view (FOV) covers porch, steps, front walk  
     – Visible to guests but blends into door frame  

  b. Living Room Ceiling Corner  
     – Flush-mount dome camera in upper corner near ceiling  
     – Paint housing the same color as ceiling or molding  
     – Angle to cover seating area, main traffic path  

  c. Kitchen / Dining Alcove  
     – Low-profile cube or bullet camera under upper cabinetry or on shelf  
     – Pointed toward sink/island and entrance to kitchen  
     – Must be in plain sight (not behind décor)  

  d. Hallway Junction  
     – Small puck-style dome at ceiling intersection  
     – Single-shot view down both hall branches  

  e. Stairwell Landing  
     – Recessed micro-dome in stairwell soffit or light fixture  
     – Covers both up/down traffic areas  

  f. Outdoor Patio / Back Door  
     – Weatherproof mini-bullet camera under eave or in porch light housing  
     – Wide angle to cover sliding door, grill area, backyard entry  

2. Technical Specifications  
   (suitable for indoor/outdoor use, low-profile mounting)

  – Video Resolution:  
      • Minimum 1080p (1920×1080) at 30 fps; 2K (2560×1440) preferred for more detail  
  – Lens & Field of View:  
      • 2.8 mm (≈100° horizontal) to 3.6 mm (≈80°) lens for balanced coverage  
      • Tilt/pan modules (optional) if you need to remotely re-frame  
  – Low-Light / Night Vision:  
      • Built-in IR LEDs for at least 5 m of usable night coverage  
      • True WDR (Wide Dynamic Range) for mixed indoor lighting  
  – Connectivity:  
      • Dual-band 2.4/5 GHz Wi-Fi (802.11ac) or PoE (Power over Ethernet) if wiring allows  
      • WPA3 or WPA2-AES encryption  
  – Storage & Recording:  
      • On-board microSD slot (≥ 64 GB), plus encrypted cloud backup  
      • Motion-triggered clips, configurable sensitivity and “privacy zones” to mask out private areas  
  – Power:  
      • PoE (802.3af) for reliable power/data over one cable  
      • If battery-powered, look for 3–6 month runtime per charge (Arlo/Flir style)  
  – Form Factor / Mounting:  
      • Flush-mount dome (Ø 75–100 mm) or micro-bullet (L≈80 mm)  
      • White or paintable housings to match ceilings/walls  

3. Example Models & Brands  
  – Indoor dome: Reolink E1 Pro (2K, pan/tilt, micro-SD + cloud)  
  – Flush mount: Hikvision DS-2CD2723G0-IZS (2K, WDR, IR, PoE)  
  – Outdoor bullet: Dahua IPC-HFW2231R-ZS (2 MP, 2.7–13.5 mm varifocal, IR, PoE)  
  – Video doorbell: Ring Video Doorbell Pro 2 (3 K, HDR, cloud subscription)  
  – Battery option (outdoor): Arlo Pro 4 (2 K, wireless, integrated siren)  

4. Installation Best Practices  
  – Height: mount at 2.2–2.5 m (7–8 ft) for optimal coverage without tampering  
  – Angle downward ~15–30° to avoid ceiling washout and maximize facial ID  
  – Secure wiring in conduits or use PoE injectors hidden in utility closets  
  – Label each camera in your in-home guide and listing (“Cameras active in living room & entryway”)  
  – Set “privacy zones” in software to mask out guestrooms or sensitive areas  

5. Software & Alerts  
  – Use a unified VMS or NVR with mobile app for live-view + push notifications  
  – Configure activity schedules (e.g. armed only when property is unoccupied)  
  – Enable geo-fencing if supported, to auto-arm when you’re away  

By following the above, you’ll achieve effective oversight of high-traffic zones—while staying fully compliant with Airbnb’s transparency rules and respecting guests’ private spaces.
